newsitem.title: JAPAN: Hertz Japan unit mulls restructuring -- source.
newsitem.headline: Hertz Japan unit mulls restructuring -- source.

text.p: The Japanese unit of U.S. rental car company Hertz Corp is considering restructuring its business, a source close to the unit said on Thursday.

A spokesman for Mazda Motor Corp, the largest shareholder in Hertz Japan Ltd, said the Japanese unit was facing diffculties and was holding discussions with its franchises about its future business plan.
Hertz Corp is 100 percent owned by Ford Motor Co and Mazda is 33.3 percent owned by Ford.

The Japanese business daily Nihon Keizai Shimbun reported on Thursday that Hertz's Japanese unit was negotiating with several Japanese firms over the sale of its rental car business rights in Japan and aiming to stop operations at the end of March.

The source close to the unit, who did not want to be identified, said the company would continue its reservation business, in which it takes reservations for rental cars abroad for customers in Japan.
The source said details of the restructuring of the rest of the unit's business were still undecided.
"Hertz Japan is facing business difficulties and it thinks it has to take measures. But it will continue the international (reservation) business," the source said.
The unit's business slump was due to severe competition, the newspaper said.
Hertz Japan posted a net loss of 500 million to 600 million yen in the year to March 31, 1996, the paper said. Its debts totalled four billion to five billion yen, the paper said.
Hertz Japan is 50 percent owned by Mazda and 17 percent by Mazda units, Hertz Japan said. It is 10 percent owned by Hertz Corp, the company said.
The Mazda spokesman said Mazda viewed the issue of Hertz Japan and its own restructuring as unrelated matters.
Earlier this month, Ford said it would review strategic opertions with respect to Hertz, which could include a partial sale of the company.
